item.title: Ukraine war briefing: Zelenskyy sees ‘window of opportunity’ for peace as US envoys to meet Putin
item.description:
Ukrainian president says he hopes Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner get ‘specifics’ from Moscow meeting after trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi. What we know on day 1,723

Volodymyr Zelenskyy said there could be a chance to reach a breakthrough this year in negotiations to end the war, as he arrived in Ireland ahead of talks with US envoys on Thursday. “Today there really is this opportunity, this window of opportunity, when all those participants who are now engaged in the negotiation process, genuinely want to achieve a result before 2027,” the Ukrainian president said. He is to meet the US presidential envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, after they return from a meeting with Russian president Vladimir Putin in Moscow. “What’s important is that the Americans flew to Putin with specifics,” Zelenskyy said. “I would very much like them to return to Dublin with specifics.”

The comments came after Russia and Ukraine agreed to the “largest prisoner exchange” of the war at their first US-brokered talks since February – but made little progress towards a broader peace agreement, reports Pjotr Sauer. Both sides sent senior delegations to the two-day talks in Abu Dhabi, led by Kushner and Witkoff. A senior member of Ukraine’s delegation said the Russian team had arrived with “very strict directives” but there had been “big progress” on postwar security guarantees for Ukraine and “I think we have good momentum to bring about a solution before the new year”. Kushner said there was no trust between ⁠the two sides but described the talks as “a good ​first step”.

Zelenskyy said Ukraine hoped for concrete results on resolving the war this year but that much depended ⁠on how ​the US approached Moscow. Speaking alongside Irish prime minister Micheál Martin on Wednesday, he said: “We are living through these massive attacks. Of course, we want to get results by ⁠the end of this year, and of course we will be doing everything ​to make that happen. A lot will ‌depend today on the format of the dialogue of the American and Russian ‌sides tomorrow.”

The head of Nato said the Abu Dhabi talks had shown that the US, Ukraine and Europe were “completely aligned and united”, stressing it was now up to Russia to show it would cooperate. “Clearly we have to see that the Russian side is willing to play ball,” Mark Rutte told reporters.

Explosions ⁠were ⁠reportedly heard in Kyiv, the Ukrainian capital, ⁠in ⁠the ​early ‌hours ‌of Thursday. In the southern Odesa region, three people died and 11 were injured after Russia launched a daytime attack on a market, local authorities said. Residential buildings were damaged, said Oleh Kiper, head of the regional military administration.

A drone attack ⁠caused a fire in the port area of Ust-Luga by the Baltic ⁠Sea in Russia’s ⁠north-west, injuring ​three workers, regional governor Aleksandr Drozdenko said on Wednesday. Ukraine later said ⁠it had launched the attack on the port, triggering a fire and damaging part ⁠of its network of fuel tanks. “According to preliminary ​information, as a result ‌of drone strikes ‌on the port’s oil infrastructure, the tank network suffered ‌the most damage,” Ukraine’s general staff said, adding that five tanks had sustained damage. A power station had also been cut off, Drozdenko said.

Ukraine says it has captured its first Indonesian prisoner of war, amid what it says is a spike in recruitment by Russia from the south-east Asian nation. Kate Lamb reports that the 49-year-old man from Java was taken to Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region to take part in a Russian assault but managed to reach Ukrainian-held territory after the group came under drone attack, according to a Ukraine’s state-run I Want to Live project. He was then captured by Ukraine.

A Ukrainian drone strike killed an employee of the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia ⁠nuclear power plant in his home in south-eastern Ukraine, the 15th to be ⁠killed since April, according to the plant’s Russian management on Wednesday.

item.title: Democrat Scott Colom wins in Mississippi to become the state’s first Black senator since Reconstruction
item.description:
Democratic nominee Scott Colom defeated Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith on Wednesday in Mississippi’s closely contested U.S. Senate race after a prolonged ballot counting process, giving the state its first Black U.S. senator since post-Civil War Reconstruction.

Colom’s narrow victory is a seismic shift in Mississippi, which has been controlled mostly by white conservatives for generations despite having the largest share of Black residents of any U.S. state. The outcome adds to a decisive midterm rebuke of President Donald Trump, whose party suffered defeats in several Republican-controlled states, and it will bolster some Democrats’ argument that their future runs through the American South.

“All I did was have the courage to imagine a night like this,” Colom told a crowd of hundreds who gathered at Tougaloo College for his victory party. “I had the courage to believe in Mississippi. I had the courage to understand that we can show the country that Mississippi matters.”

The Associated Press called the race in Colom’s favor after local officials spent several days processing absentee and provisional ballots, called affidavit ballots in Mississippi.

The last time Mississippi chose a new Democratic senator was 1947; the winner was a staunch segregationist. Colom, a 43-year-old local prosecutor, capitalized on the state’s large Black population, discontent with the economy and Hyde-Smith’s missteps as she sought a second full term.

“They actually deserve a senator that will listen to them, that actually cares about what they think, actually cares about what they’re going through,” Colom said in the campaign’s closing stretch.

Hyde-Smith, 67, called Colom late Wednesday afternoon to concede and released a concession speech online shortly afterward.

“While this is not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters,” Hyde-Smith said. “I want to congratulate Scott Colom and wish him well as he takes on the tremendous responsibility of representing our great state.”

Colom said during the campaign that he could represent all of Mississippi, a state where racial divisions have long defined its politics and society, and he repeated that pledge after his victory.

“My commitment to you, each and every one of you, is that first I’m going to treat your children like I want my children to be treated,” Colom said. “I’m going to treat your parents the way I want my parents to be treated. I’m gonna treat your future the way I want my future to be” and “work to make every Mississippian’s life better.”

National Democrats, activists and Mississippians celebrate

Party leaders hailed the senator-elect’s triumph, with nods to the South’s emerging status as a political battleground after other victories from North Carolina and South Carolina to Georgia and Texas.

“Scott ran the campaign of a lifetime and re-imagined what’s possible for Democrats in the South,” Democratic Senate leader Chuck Schumer of New York posted online.

Former President Bill Clinton, a native Arkansan who campaigned with Colom days before the election, addressed the senator-elect on social media, saying he won “because you believe in the promise of your state’s people. And they believed in you right back.”

Vera Finley was among those supporters.

“I am here to celebrate my parents and my grandparents. I am not one generation out of the cotton fields,” Finley said ahead of Colom’s victory speech. “Both of my parents picked cotton. And my great-grandmother was sold here as a slave from Virginia to here. So I am so excited to be on this side of history.”

Another Mississippian, NAACP President Derrick Johnson, issued a statement saying the state’s voters, most notably Black voters, “made history because they refused to be intimidated, discouraged, or counted out” in a state that has seen “some of the nation’s most difficult battles for voting rights.”

A race Washington once viewed as a long shot

The contest was a latecomer to the national spotlight, finally drawing attention and money months after Black senators, including Georgia’s Raphael Warnock and Maryland’s Angela Alsobrooks, first urged donors and party leaders to see it as winnable.

The son of a onetime Republican who worked for President Ronald Reagan, Colom produced one of the year’s most widely circulated ads. After Hyde-Smith seemed to brush off high beef prices by saying consumers could choose other proteins, Colom cut a 30-second spot depicting incredulous voters saying they’d “pick another senator instead.”

When Trump came to Corinth, Mississippi, in late October to rally with Hyde-Smith, Colom walked the line of Trump supporters as they waited to enter. He introduced himself and asked about their concerns.

Later, when Trump called Hyde-Smith to the stage, she said only nine words in six seconds before stepping away: “Is this not the best president in our lifetime?”

Colom’s appearance outside the rally tracked his strategy of criticizing Trump’s policies — especially the Iran war that drove up gas prices and tariffs that caused headaches for Mississippi farmers — without taking personal jabs at the president or people who voted for him. Instead, he consistently put the onus on Hyde-Smith, framing her as a nonentity in Washington — a critique that resonated in a state accustomed to long-serving, powerful senators.

There is some irony in Hyde-Smith losing to Colom. In 2022, President Joe Biden nominated Colom to be a U.S. District Court judge. Mississippi’s senior Republican Sen. Roger Wicker and former Gov. Haley Barbour, who is also a former national Republican chairman, backed the nomination.

Hyde-Smith, however, blocked Colom’s confirmation. Colom said his campaign was never about getting even with Hyde-Smith.

Colom called on Mississippi’s history

The senator-elect concluded his campaign with an ad that featured him at the Jackson home of Medgar Evers, the civil rights leader who, in 1963, was gunned down in his driveway by a white supremacist.

Colom told the story of Evers’ military service at Normandy in World War II, his voter registration efforts in Mississippi, his assassination and the three decades it took to win a conviction. “He was killed for helping Mississippians vote,” Colom said. “On Tuesday, use your vote and honor everyone who died for that right.”

At the lectern Wednesday night, Colom said it was appropriate that the race be called on Veterans Day, as he again paid tribute to Evers.

“He served his country, came home to Mississippi, and they wouldn’t let him vote,” Colom said. “But he had faith that Mississippi could make progress.”

Despite Republicans’ domination, the path was always there

Because of the Black population and its alignment with Democrats, Mississippi’s general elections have been closer for years than its Southern neighbors. Trump won by double digits in each of his three presidential contests, but in 2023, Republican Gov. Tate Reeves managed to win reelection by a margin of just 3 percentage points.

Colom and other Black party leaders and strategists insisted throughout 2026 that he could narrow the gap with strong Black turnout, Republican discontent and an uptick in Democrats’ usual share of the white vote in Mississippi.

Results showed strong turnout in the Mississippi Delta and its concentration of majority Black counties. But nearly all of the state moved leftward from the 2024 election, when Trump carried Mississippi by nearly 23 points.

Hyde-Smith was appointed to the Senate in 2018. She won a special election runoff in 2018 and a full term in 2020. Both times she defeated Democrat Mike Espy, a former U.S. agriculture secretary who’d also been Mississippi’s first Black congressman since Reconstruction.

During the extended vote count, Colom acknowledged the historic nature of his candidacy but said he cares more about what it means for others.

“My job is to do well enough as the next United States senator that the next time some young Black boy or girl has the work ethic, the vision and the values,” he said, “and they want to be United States senator, that nobody says because of anything I’ve done that they shouldn’t get a chance.”

—Bill Barrow and Sophie Bates, Associated Press

item.title: Ukraine war briefing: Europe to join negotiations, says Kushner, as Putin warns against peace keepers
item.description:
Jared Kushner says move will allow talks to address ‘broader postwar European security arrangements’; Putin refuses to soften territorial demands. What we know on day 1,724

Ukraine and Russia have agreed to expand the next round of peace negotiations to include European countries, Donald Trump’s envoy and son-in-law Jared Kushner said late on Thursday, after meeting Russian president Vladimir Putin. “This will allow us to address the broader postwar European security arrangements alongside the territorial issues between Ukraine and Russia,” Kushner ​said ​later on X. “We are also working toward ‌what would be the largest prisoner ​exchange of the war, potentially reuniting thousands of people ⁠with their families.”

After the Moscow meeting, Kushner and Witkoff flew ⁠to Ireland to attend a European summit and meet Zelenskyy, who said he was pleased at the prospect of European participation in talks and said he hoped the agenda would include steps towards a ceasefire and de-escalating the conflict. “We decided that we will work on an agenda about any kind of de-escalation, some kind of ceasefires,” Zelenskyy said after meeting the US envoys. “I hope that we will have such agenda,” he said.

Putin warned Europe not to send peacekeeping troops into Ukraine in the event of a peace deal saying it was a “continuation of war”. Putin also refused to soften his territorial demands and said Washington must work with its European allies to understand if they want peace or war in Ukraine.

Putin’s comments underlined how ⁠difficult the negotiations could become, given sharp differences between Moscow ​and European capitals over the way the war should end. “The Europeans will join at the next meeting, which we consider to be a very important moment because they are our partners and it’s important to us that they take part,” Witkoff told Russian state TV after meeting Putin in the Kremlin.

Kushner told Putin Washington had detected what he called “a big change” on the European side and was confident that expanding peace talks to include the Europeans would not hinder progress. Putin said Moscow had always been open to talking to the EU about Ukraine, but ​signalled serious outstanding differences. “As far as the Europeans are concerned, we have never been opposed to engaging in dialogue ‌with Europe, and we have never broken off that dialogue. It was ‌they who broke off the dialogue with the Russian Federation,” he said. “We would very much like you, gentlemen, and the US administration as a whole, to work with your European allies so that they can finally make up their minds as to what they want: peace or war in Ukraine,” said Putin.

However, Zelenskyy said new restrictions were affecting the US-made satellite communications Kyiv uses on the battlefield, and that he found the US approach of discussing a new European security order with Russia “a bit strange”. Earlier on Thursday, he said disruptions to the Starshield satellite ​communications service had affected the entire frontline and Russian-controlled parts of Ukraine. Starshield is the military version of SpaceX’s Starlink satellite communications service, and Ukraine suffered similar disruptions last month. “So far we know very little (on the Starshield restrictions). But some things are already clear: if someone in America is making decisions that basically treat Ukrainian territory as if it is not Ukrainian, then it tells us where things are going,” he said. SpaceX declined to comment.

During the talks, the conflict between the two countries continued. A Russian drone ⁠strike killed two people in the ⁠northern ⁠Ukrainian ​region of Sumy, Governor Oleh Hryhorov said ⁠on Telegram late on Thursday, while in Rivne ⁠in the north-west, ​five ‌people were injured ‌after a Russian drone hit ‌an apartment building, a local Ukrainian official said on Telegram early on Friday. In Russia’s ‌Belgorod region bordering Ukraine, a man ​was killed and another four injured in a drone attack, ⁠local officials said on Telegram ​on ​Thursday. item.title: Ukraine war briefing: US proposes Kyiv cede land to Russia for Nato membership, Zelenskyy says
item.description:
Ukrainian president says Kyiv not ready to concede Donbas but would put idea to a referendum in exchange for security guarantees and funding. What we know on day 1,726

Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said the US has asked for the first time if Ukraine would withdraw from parts of the eastern Donbas region that Russia does not control in exchange for Ukraine becoming a Nato member. But the Ukrainian president said his country would not surrender territory. “The Americans raised a question: ‘What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?’,” he said in remarks to reporters released by his office on Saturday. “That is why ⁠I believe Nato is back on the agenda.” But he said the suggestion, which would form part of a new postwar security framework for Europe, could allow Russia to weaken Nato and reshape borders. “This is dangerous because, in my view, it is precisely things like this that lead to wars or escalations,” Zelenskyy said.

Zelenskyy reiterated his position that Kyiv was not ready to concede territory but said that if it received a comprehensive package including security guarantees, the right to a strong and well-funded ​Ukrainian army and funds to rebuild, he would put the question to a ‌national referendum. Echoing comments ‌made by European leaders at a summit in Dublin on Friday, Zelenskyy dismissed Russia’s call for a broad agreement on European security architecture to be reached before the specifics are ‌agreed on how to end the war in Ukraine. “We cannot turn everything upside down and start by talking about changing the security framework in the world or across the continent overall, and only then talk about ending this war. This war must be ended first,” he said.

The Ukrainian president has also rejected the possibility of Ukraine committing to neutrality, something that could only happen if the country’s constitution was changed. “If Putin expects Ukraine’s neutrality to be enshrined, that’s not going to happen,” he said. “We’re not in Nato right now anyway.”

US President ⁠Donald Trump’s ⁠envoy and ​son-in-law Jared ⁠Kushner said on ⁠Saturday ​the US ‌was ‌focused on ‌facilitating direct engagement between Russia and ‌European nations on ​the Ukraine war, ⁠after trilateral meetings ​involving Washington, ​Moscow ​and ​Kyiv ‌this ​week. However, Washington and Nato have not yet commented on the suggestion of a swap of the Donbas for Ukraine Nato membership. Negotiations did, however, lead to agreements that European countries would join future talks on ending the war.

Zelenskyy has accused SpaceX of not telling the truth over restrictions to Ukraine’s Starshield satellite system, saying the decision to impose speed limits appears to be “political” rather than “technical”. Speaking on Friday, Ukraine’s president said the restrictions affecting Ukrainian drones, in place for five days, meant they could no longer intercept incoming jet-powered Russian Shahed drones. Ukraine suspects the slowdown is a deliberate US tactic, designed to put pressure on Zelenskyy to make concessions to Putin.

French President Emmanuel Macron said Saturday that countries seeking to limit aid to Ukraine want to impose an “unjust peace” and warned that it was a recipe for another war. “Those who want to ration aid to Ukraine wish underneath it all to force an unjust peace on it” and, by extension, all of Europe, Macron said on social media. “That is a recipe for another war. That cannot be France’s position.”

Russian forces ⁠struck a cargo vessel in ⁠the ⁠Ukrainian ​port of Chornomorsk, RIA ⁠news agency cited the Russian ⁠defence ministry ​as ‌saying on ‌Saturday. The ministry ‌said the ship was being used to supply the Ukrainian ‌military. Meanwhile, Ukrainian strikes on the Samara oil pipeline station near the village of Prosvet in Russia’s Samara region on Friday set several oil storage tanks on fire, Ukraine’s General Staff said. The facility is a key part of the network exporting Russian oil to global markets, the General Staff said. item.title: Grocery giant Aldi recalls tortelloni over potentially ‘life-threatening’ health risks: Avoid these products
item.description:
Aldi has issued a recall due to the potential presence of Clostridium botulinum. 

Two tortellini products from the Illinois-based grocery store chain’s Priano brand might contain the life-threatening bacteria, according to a recall notice from Aldi that was reposted by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

Clostridium botulinum, or C. botulinum, can cause botulism, a very dangerous form of food poisoning.

According to the notice, the potential contamination resulted because the products may have been stored, distributed, or sold at improper temperatures.  

Here’s what you need to know about the Aldi recall. 

What products are affected?

The Aldi recall is for two types of its tortellini:

Priano Protein Carbonara Tortelloni, 9 oz, plastic unit 

  • Lot number: T9101926
  • Best-by date: December 18, 2026

Priano Protein Herb & Cheese Tortelloni, 9 oz, plastic unit

  • Lot number: T9101926
  • Best-by date: December 18, 2026

Where and when was the product sold?

The announcement doesn’t say exactly when the tortellini products were sold, but we do know where. Aldi sold the recalled products in-store and online from stores in the following states:

  • Alabama
  • Georgia
  • North Carolina 
  • South Carolina

What should I do if I have this product? 

You should either throw out the recalled tortellini or return it to Aldi for a full refund. “Consumers are warned not to prepare or consume the affected products from the impacted states, even if they do not look or smell spoiled,” the announcement states.

You can contact Aldi with any questions at (844) 484-0332 from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. ET, Monday to Friday. 

What botulism signs should I look out for? 

Get medical attention immediately if you’ve eaten the recalled tortellini and experience any of the following symptoms of botulism: 

  • Abdominal distension
  • Constipation
  • Difficulty breathing
  • Dizziness
  • Double vision
  • General weakness
  • Muscle weakness
  • Trouble speaking or swallowing

item.title: KFC store closures: See the full list of doomed restaurant locations as a large franchisee files for bankruptcy
item.description:
Bad news for fried chicken fans.

Dozens of KFC restaurants have closed or will close their doors soon after their owner sought Chapter 11 protection this week—part of a wave of recent bankruptcies involving leveraged fast-food franchisees.

The franchisee, Tasty Chick’n LLC, operated 75 KFC restaurants and another nine cobranded KFC/Taco Bell locations across 10 states at the time of its bankruptcy petition.

But it also disclosed a list of more than 70 restaurants whose operations it did not deem worthy of continuing.

Those restaurants—many of which appear to have closed before the bankruptcy petition—are located in Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Missouri, Mississippi, Tennessee, and Virginia.

The Memphis area appears especially hard hit, with more than a dozen of the city’s KFC locations on the closure list.

Why did the franchisee file for bankruptcy?

Texas-based Tasty Chick’n and its affiliates say higher operating costs and declining revenue have eaten into their bottom line, with restaurant-level profitability declining since 2023. 

At the same time, the franchisee says costly demands for store upgrades from Yum Brands—parent company of KFC and Taco Bell—have led to $15.6 million in unpaid royalties owed to the restaurant giant.

The situation became so precarious that Yum Brands in September sent Tasty Chick’n a “notice of intent” to terminate the company’s franchise agreements, court filings say. The franchisee turned to the Chapter 11 process with the hope of selling its assets while it explores “other stand-alone restructuring alternatives.”

Fast Company reached out to Yum Brands and Tasty Chick’n for comment.

Which KFC restaurants have closed or are closing?

In court papers filed on Tuesday, Tasty Chick’n listed dozens of its restaurants that it says are closing soon, in the process of closing, or have already closed.

A cursory search of the addresses reveals that most of the stores are already marked as closed on Google, with some of the closures happening recently.

The company and its affiliates are now seeking court permission to get out of their lease obligations for the locations and abandon the properties.

Tasty Chick’n is managed by Tasty Restaurant Group (TRG), which oversees a sprawling empire of fast food restaurants across the South, Midwest, and Northeast—a fleet that includes Burger King, Pizza Hut, and Dunkin’ locations, in addition to KFC and Taco Bell. TRG is not identified as a debtor in the Chapter 11 proceedings.

Why does this sound familiar? 

Tasty Chick’n is not the first large fast-food restaurant operator to seek Chapter 11 protection this year.

In September, the owner of more than 300 Wendy’s restaurants filed for bankruptcy after years of sales struggles and a contentious relationship with the chain’s parent company. Franchisees for Denny’s, Subway, Moe’s Southwest Grill, and others have made similar moves.

Collectively, these franchisees have closed hundreds of restaurants in 2026.

Is KFC in trouble?

It’s not having the best year. Yum Brands recently reported a third-quarter decline of 6% for KFC’s U.S. sales. The picture is rosier elsewhere in the world, particularly in markets like the Middle East and Asia, where KFC’s Q3 sales were up by double digits.

The brand has faced increased competition in the market, particularly among younger consumers who have gravitated toward trendier chains such as Dave’s Hot Chicken and Raising Cane’s.

item.title: Chase confirms cyberattack that may have exposed customer data. Here’s what we know
item.description:
Chase Bank isn’t doing much to reassure customers.

The bank said Thursday that third-party vendors were recently targeted in a cyberattack that resulted in a breach of some customer information. But there is “no connection” between this cyber attack and the outage earlier this week that saw customers unable to log in to their accounts, the bank posted on X.

“Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses,” Chase said in the post, without specifying when the breach occurred.

JPMorgan Chase, parent company of the bank, was one of several financial institutions to experience outages on Monday that saw many customers unable to log in to their accounts for several hours. A string of high-profile outages in the past week has upended work and air travel, while keeping Americans locked out of various websites. Even a highly classified network for internal communications at the National Security Agency also experienced an outage.

Another day, another data breach shouldn’t surprise most Americans at this point. But paranoia has been proliferating online about a more coordinated takedown of our tech infrastructure—and even though Chase said the cyberattack and outage are unrelated, some people aren’t buying what the largest U.S. bank is saying.

The New York-based company previously blamed the disruptions on Monday on a “software bug” that was resolved and said there was no evidence of a cyberattack or a systemic issue. 

So to announce a cyberattack a few days later has only raised more questions. A spokesperson for JPMorganChase didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment from Fast Company.

Cybernews reported Thursday that the ransomware gang n0n dumped on the dark web the stolen data of some 16,000 JPMorganChase customers and employees on Thursday after a 48-hour ransom had passed. The hackers said it had allegedly stolen information related to Chase’s premium Reserve credit card program that’s marketed to affluent Americans, as the outlet reported.

The most popular comment on a subreddit discussing that news report came from a Redditor who posted: “We are being lied to by the government.” That sort of refrain has become increasingly common as people have become more paranoid that something more nefarious is happening. 

RUBIO TRIES TO REASSURE

As conspiracy theories have flourished online in the wake of these outages, that’s led some Americans to panic-buying items at Costco, as Bloomberg reported. Meanwhile, a petition on Change.org to “demand full transparency” about these recent tech disruptions has yet to garner much support.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio has seemingly taken on the task in the Trump administration of trying to calm the nerves of Americans. Speaking on Tuesday during a trip to Asia with President Donald Trump, Rubio said the government has “no evidence” of a link between the outages or that they’re the result of cyberattacks, as Politico reported. 

“We fully acknowledge that this is unsettling to see these reports day after day of some technical failures,” Rubio told reporters on Tuesday. “We have no evidence, no indications of any kind that these incidents are related to each other or that any of them have anything to do with a malign actor, with a cyber criminal.”
